title: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, its fourth Flash model in under four month
content:
September 2, 2026
Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, its fourth Flash model in under four months
See model page
Gemini 3.8 Flash scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and reaches the Intelligence vs. Cost per Task Pareto frontier
Google DeepMind released Gemini 3.8 Flash today. With high reasoning, it scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, up 3 points from Gemini 3.7 Flash and on par with sub-maximum reasoning efforts of GPT-5.6 Sol (xhigh, 59) and Grok 4.6 (medium, 59)
Matching Gemini 3.7 Flash’s discounted pricing until the end of the year ($0.75/$3.75 per million input/output tokens), Gemini 3.8 Flash sits on the Intelligence vs. Cost per Task Pareto frontier at $0.58 per task. This is comparable to GPT-5.6 Terra (max, $0.53), but ~40% higher than its predecessor, driven by a 30% increase in average output tokens per task to 48k and increased turns on agentic evaluations
Key benchmarking results across Gemini 3.8 Flash’s three reasoning levels:
➤ 3 point Intelligence Index improvement: Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, up 3 points from Gemini 3.7 Flash (high, 56). With medium reasoning it scores 57, matching GPT-5.6 Terra (max, 57) and Muse Spark 1.2 (xhigh, 57). With low reasoning it scores 52, matching Gemini 3.6 Flash (high, 52), at 30% lower Cost per Task and roughly a third of the Time per Task
➤ Agentic capability improvements: Gemini 3.8 Flash’s 3 point improvement on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is primarily driven by stronger performance on agentic evaluations such as 𝜏³-Banking (tool use), Terminal-Bench v2.1 (coding) and GDPval-AA v2 (real-world tasks). The largest improvement is on 𝜏³-Banking, where it gains 12 points over Gemini 3.7 Flash to score 45%
➤ Pareto frontier on Intelligence vs. Cost per Task: Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) costs $0.58 per Intelligence Index task, making it the cheapest model at its level of intelligence. This is up ~40% from Gemini 3.7 Flash ($0.40) despite unchanged per-token pricing, driven by a 30% increase in output tokens per task and more turns on agentic evaluations. Cost per Task falls to $0.41 with medium reasoning and $0.24 with low reasoning
➤ Output speeds remain fast, but Time per Task increases: On high reasoning, Gemini 3.8 Flash averages ~300 output tokens per second and a Time per Task of 2.5 minutes, slightly faster than GPT-5.6 Luna (max, 2.6 minutes) and GPT-5.6 Terra (max, 3.3). Compared to Gemini 3.7 Flash, higher token usage increases Time per Task from 2.2 minutes to 2.5 minutes, and puts it behind Claude Fable 5.1 (medium, 2.1 minutes). On low reasoning, Time per Task falls to 0.8 minutes, placing Gemini 3.8 Flash on the Intelligence vs. Time per Task Pareto frontier
Key model details:
➤ Context Window: 1M tokens, unchanged from Gemini 3.7 Flash
➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output
➤ Pricing: $0.75/$3.75 per 1M input/output tokens through the end of the year, matching Gemini 3.7 Flash’s current discounted pricing. $1.50/$7.50 per 1M input/output tokens at standard pricing. Cached input tokens retain the same 90% discount

report.summary: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash, scoring 59 on AI Intelligence Index and reaching the cost-per-task Pareto frontier with agentic gains.
report.background: Gemini 3.8 Flash is the fourth Flash model Google DeepMind has shipped in under four months, reflecting a rapidly accelerating release cadence in small, cost-efficient models. It follows Gemini 3.7 Flash and competes directly with GPT-5.6, Grok 4.6, Claude Fable 5.1, and Muse Spark variants. The Flash line targets developers who want frontier-adjacent intelligence without flagship pricing. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Gemini 3.8 Flash scores 59 with high reasoning — up three points from its predecessor and comparable to sub-maximum GPT-5.6 and medium-reasoning Grok. It also lands on the Intelligence vs. Cost per Task Pareto frontier, meaning no other model delivers its intelligence level more cheaply per benchmark task. However, per-task cost rose about 40% even though token prices stayed flat, because the model now emits more output tokens and takes more turns on agentic evaluations. That tradeoff is central to this release.
key_points: Gemini 3.8 Flash with high reasoning scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, three points higher than Gemini 3.7 Flash and on par with GPT-5.6 Sol at sub-maximum reasoning and Grok 4.6 at medium reasoning. Medium reasoning scores 57, while low reasoning scores 52.

Despite unchanged discounted token pricing, cost per task rose roughly 40% to $0.58 because average output tokens per task increased 30% and agentic evaluations need more turns. It is nevertheless the cheapest model at its intelligence level and sits on the Pareto frontier.

The intelligence gain is driven mainly by agentic improvements. Gemini 3.8 Flash makes its largest jump on tau3-Banking, rising 12 points to 45%, with additional gains on Terminal-Bench v2.1 for coding and GDPval-AA v2 for real-world task performance.

Output speed remains near 300 tokens per second on high reasoning, but Time per Task increases from 2.2 to 2.5 minutes because the model uses more tokens. Low reasoning cuts Time per Task to 0.8 minutes and puts the model on the speed frontier.

Key specifications are unchanged: a 1M-token context window and text, image, video, and speech input with text output. Pricing stays at $0.75/$3.75 per million input/output tokens through year-end, with standard pricing double that and a 90% cache read discount.
report.impact: This launch accelerates the trend of pushing near-frontier intelligence into cheap, fast models. Developers get three explicit reasoning levels to balance capability, cost, and latency, and the agentic gains make Flash viable for tool use, coding, and multistep tasks previously reserved for large models. But because per-task token use is rising, budgets based only on per-token prices will understate real spending. For regular users, Gemini becomes more capable without headline price hikes, though high-reasoning responses may take a bit longer. Low-reasoning mode offers a strong speed and value option. The broader market effect is that frontier-level intelligence is becoming commodity-grade, pressuring standalone API providers and making independent benchmarking more central to model choice.
report.tools: To follow up, watch Google AI Studio and the Gemini API for rollouts, and Artificial Analysis for live benchmark comparisons. Open-source evaluators like Terminal-Bench and tau3-bench expose agentic coding and tool-use strengths. Developers can also use LangChain or LlamaIndex with Gemini to test tool-calling, or track cross-model pricing on OpenRouter.
